label: conj:bar-parity-split
title: The binding trace and the $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ residue are the bar-even and bar-odd parts of one fibre element
html:
There is a fibre element F, specified independently of the binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta data, such that the binding trace is read off the bar-even part of F and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue is read off its bar-odd part.

Here the parity is taken with respect to the bar-involution \sigma, q \mapsto q^{-1}, \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id} (Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections), and the even and odd parts are x + \sigma x and x - \sigma x (Even/odd decomposition under a linear involution). The binding trace is \tau = \mathrm{tr}\, B of Symplectic prolongation (det B = 1) gives a one-parameter recurrence; it is bar-even, being a function of (q+q^{-1})/2 = \cosh\lambda.

Status of the two sides. The decomposition lemma holds for every element of every module with an involution, so it does not by itself support the conjecture. The content lies in the identification of the two readouts. When F ranges over the same space as the readouts and both readouts are the identity, a suitable F exists if and only if the binding trace is bar-even and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue is bar-odd: the sum of the two is such an F, and conversely the odd part of any element is \sigma-anti. None of the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta trace functionals on record is bar-odd. Each carries the factor h = q - q^{-1} = 2\sinh\lambda and vanishes at q = 1, which is a weaker property. The conjecture therefore requires a specified element F with readout maps other than the identity, and no such F has yet been given. For the nucleon element used for \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, the natural candidate F = \mathfrak{n} - \mathfrak{p} with the Markov trace as readout fails as well. The trace intertwines the bar-involution with q \mapsto q^{-1}, and the readout factors as h\,g, where g is the trace of the remaining context words. The readout is therefore bar-odd if and only if g is bar-even, and here g is not.

Relation to the complex volume. If the conjecture holds, the bar-even/bar-odd split is a candidate for the real/imaginary split of the complex volume \mathfrak{V} of Complex-volume unification. Under the continuation \lambda \mapsto i\theta, \cosh\lambda \mapsto \cos\theta and \sinh\lambda \mapsto i\sin\theta, so a bar-even part would continue to a real quantity and a bar-odd part to an imaginary one.
heading: Conjecture
